standard_prerequisites.name: Tensoring commutes with pushouts
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used in the middle of the counted proof (lines 21173-21179)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the kernel sequence after tensoring with an arbitrary module, which is what compares the two conditions.

core_obligations: Recall the description of the pushout and derive from it the short exact sequence relating the kernels of f, g and f' (proof lines 21166-21172).
Tensor that sequence with an arbitrary module Q, using that tensoring commutes with pushouts, to obtain the corresponding sequence of tensored kernels (proof lines 21173-21179).
Read off the equivalence: the kernel of f' after tensoring vanishes exactly when the kernel of f after tensoring sits inside that of g, which is domination (proof lines 21180-21182).
proof_roadmap: Describe the pushout and its kernel sequence (proof lines 21165-21172).
Tensor with an arbitrary module and translate injectivity of the pushout map into the domination condition (proof lines 21173-21183).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for maps f and g out of a common module M, the map g dominates f exactly when the pushout map f' is universally injective (statement lines 21152-21163, with the pushout square drawn in the statement). The proof does not construct the dominating factorisation: it recalls that the pushout is a quotient of a direct sum, writes down the resulting short exact sequence of kernels of f, g and f', transports it along tensoring with an arbitrary module using that tensoring commutes with pushouts, and then reads the two conditions off the same sequence (proof lines 21165-21183). Getting both sides into one kernel sequence is the content of the argument. H2.
